title: What Is Hiding in the Gold?

pages.text: Madam Ayim put on her lab coat and held up a photograph of a small gold bead. “Gold is beautiful,” she said, “and it is one of Ghana’s great resources. But the way some people get it can harm us for years. Today we study what is hiding in the gold. Please do not copy any of this at home. This is science for understanding, not instructions.”
sentences: Madam Ayim put on her lab coat and held up a photograph of a small gold bead.
“Gold is beautiful,” she said, “and it is one of Ghana’s great resources.
But the way some people get it can harm us for years.
Today we study what is hiding in the gold.
Please do not copy any of this at home.
This is science for understanding, not instructions.”
pages.alt: A teacher holds up a photograph of a small gold bead in front of a class wearing goggles.

pages.text: “In small-scale mining, some miners mix crushed ore with mercury,” said Madam Ayim. “Mercury is a liquid metal that sticks to tiny gold flecks and forms a lump called an amalgam. Then the amalgam is heated, the mercury turns to vapour, and the gold is left behind. Human Rights Watch reported in 2014 that mercury was sold openly in shops in Ghana.”

“Mercury is a liquid metal that sticks to tiny gold flecks and forms a lump called an amalgam.
Then the amalgam is heated, the mercury turns to vapour, and the gold is left behind.
Human Rights Watch reported in 2014 that mercury was sold openly in shops in Ghana.”
pages.alt: A diagram: ore, a liquid metal, a lump called amalgam and a heated dish releasing vapour.

pages.text: “Where does the mercury go?” asked Nabila. “That is the problem,” said Madam Ayim. “When it is heated, the vapour can be breathed in by the miner, and sometimes by family members if the burning is done at home. When it is washed away, it settles in rivers and soil. Mercury is an element, so it cannot be destroyed. It only moves.”
sentences: “Where does the mercury go?” asked Nabila.
“That is the problem,” said Madam Ayim.
“When it is heated, the vapour can be breathed in by the miner, and sometimes by family members if the burning is done at home.
When it is washed away, it settles in rivers and soil.
Mercury is an element, so it cannot be destroyed.
It only moves.”
pages.alt: Arrows showing vapour drifting from a burning dish and liquid flowing from a washing pit to a river.

pages.text: “In the river,” said Madam Ayim, “bacteria can change mercury into a form that living things absorb easily. Small animals take it in. Small fish eat them. Bigger fish eat the small fish. At each step the mercury builds up. We call this bioaccumulation. People who eat the fish take it in too.” Selom drew the food chain on the board with arrows.
sentences: “In the river,” said Madam Ayim, “bacteria can change mercury into a form that living things absorb easily.
Small animals take it in.
Small fish eat them.
Bigger fish eat the small fish.
At each step the mercury builds up.
We call this bioaccumulation.
People who eat the fish take it in too.” Selom drew the food chain on the board with arrows.
pages.alt: A food chain drawing: bacteria, small animals, small fish, big fish, a person, with the mercury level rising at each step.

pages.text: “What does mercury do to us?” asked Selom. “It can damage the nervous system, including the brain, and the kidneys and heart. Children are especially at risk, because their bodies are still growing. For pregnant women, it can put the unborn baby at risk,” said Madam Ayim. “Doctors in Ghana have also warned about other metals, such as lead, cadmium and arsenic, in mining areas.”

For pregnant women, it can put the unborn baby at risk,” said Madam Ayim.
“Doctors in Ghana have also warned about other metals, such as lead, cadmium and arsenic, in mining areas.”
pages.alt: A simple body outline highlighting the brain, kidneys and heart, with a small child and a pregnant woman nearby.

pages.text: “Let us be careful about what we know,” said Madam Ayim. “A team of Ghanaian scientists found heavy metals in placentas from mothers in galamsey areas. But doctors also say it is only logical to suspect kidney harm in children, because adult studies show it. Warnings are not the same as proof. We need more studies, and we should act carefully while we wait.”

But doctors also say it is only logical to suspect kidney harm in children, because adult studies show it.
Warnings are not the same as proof.
We need more studies, and we should act carefully while we wait.”
pages.alt: A chart with two columns: What studies show / What doctors warn, with a question mark between them.

pages.text: “Is there a safer way?” asked Nabila. “Yes,” said Madam Ayim. “Gold can be separated by methods that do not use mercury, such as gravity separation. Researchers at a Ghanaian university have also developed a device called the Lantern Retort, which traps mercury vapour so that less of it escapes. Better still is mercury-free processing, and strict control of mercury sales.”

pages.alt: A diagram of gravity separation in a sloping channel and a closed retort device.

pages.text: The pupils wrote questions for a visiting doctor: “How can families get tested? What should a mother do if she lives near a mining site?” Madam Ayim smiled. “Science asks questions,” she said, “and then it asks what we should do. Gold can shine without poisoning the people who live around it.” The end.

activities.question: Why does mercury not just disappear when it is heated or washed away?
options: It is an element that cannot be destroyed, only moved

activities.prompt: Mercury builds up as it moves up the food chain. Who might have the most?
options: Big fish and people who eat them

activities.question: What does Madam Ayim say about warnings and proof?
options: Warnings are not the same as proof, so we need more studies and care

activities.definition: The build-up of a harmful substance in living things as it moves up the food chain.

activities.prompt: Put the mercury journey in order.
items: Mercury is used to catch gold.
Mercury enters the river or the air.
Small animals and fish absorb it.
People who eat contaminated fish take it in.

activities.prompt: Learning about hidden dangers can be worrying. What helps you stay calm and act wisely?

glossary.definition: A heavy, silvery liquid metal that is poisonous to people.
A mixture of mercury with another metal, such as gold.
A gas formed when a liquid or solid is heated.
The build-up of a harmful substance in living things.
A closed container that heats a substance and traps the gas it gives off.
